title: How to Replace a Steam Radiator: Hand Valve, Spud, and Radiator Sizing
summary: This Old House demonstrates diagnosing a cold room caused by an undersized steam radiator in a single-zone system, then removing an existing radiator, upgrading the hand valve and spud, and installing a correctly sized radiator to restore even heat. The walkthrough emphasizes radiator balance as key to heat distribution, and it provides practical plumbing and machining techniques (three-corner bite, spud wrench) along with leak-prevention steps (pipe dope, wicking) and a safety-conscious test after reassembly.

sections.title: System balance and radiator sizing basics
sections.description: Intro discusses four bedrooms, a plan to heat rooms adequately, and why matching radiator size to load matters in a single-zone steam system.

sections.title: Safety prep and removal readiness
sections.description: Explains shutting off power, keeping the radiator level to allow drainage, and notes floor settling with shim usage.

sections.title: Replacing hand valve and preparing spud
sections.description: Shows installing a new hand valve and discusses the spud and its tabs, including reuse of the existing spud when possible.

sections.title: Sealing joints: pipe dope and wicking
sections.description: Demonstrates applying pipe joint sealant and wick to joints to minimize leaks during reassembly and testing.
